narratives.Overview:
## Bound-remedy (next-build, successor lean 5650036623)

- Restate item 1 as (a) stale stderr literal vbrief at session-start-hook.ts:88 and (b) code 2 for no-active-xBRIEF is a normal state, not session-start-degraded.
- Do not add a playbook note that You are not authenticated does not mean what it says. Presence of auth.json is not a live session.
- occupancy:grant --help is the occupancy-namespace parse shape, not one verb. Either dispatcher-wide --help or the error names deft help / deft commands.
- Drop the inner recovery append at verify-session-ritual.ts:404-409. That is the one edit that fixes hook and CLI without regressing other branches.

Do not implement sibling 4410/4409. Do not tell maintainers to ignore You are not authenticated.

## Original issue body (superseded; do not implement as Expected)

Four small defects found while driving Grok Build against Directive 0.114.0. None blocks work; each costs a reader or a maintainer time, and the last one will send a new maintainer into a login loop.

Environment: Directive 0.114.0 · Grok Build 1.0.25 · Claude Code · win32 · consumer repo with Directive installed.

---

## 1. SessionStart probes the legacy `vbrief/` path and reports exit 2 every session

Every session begins with this injected into agent context:

> Directive SessionStart bookkeeping reported exit 2 on its non-blocking path: `_session_start_hook.py: no active vBRIEF found under vbrief/active/; skipping sentinel write.`

The installer creates `xbrief/`, and `deft doctor` confirms the migration is complete:

```
xBrief migration: none -- xbrief active, vbrief removed.
```

So the hook probes a directory the same install deliberately removed, and reports a non-zero exit for its absence. Reproduced in two separate checkouts, and visible in this repository's own session-start context.

It is non-blocking, but "reported exit 2" is the first thing an agent reads at session start, and it reads as a fault.

## 2. Denial text duplicates its recovery sentence

```
Directive denied write: session ritual gated step 'doctor' failed: [deft doctor] status: dirty (exit 1)
Recovery: run deft session:ready (one-shot: session:start + gated ritual + cache recovery as needed).
Recovery: run deft session:ready (one-shot: session:start + gated ritual + cache recovery as needed).
payloadRoot=… effectiveRoot=…
```

Looks like the gated-step reason and the envelope each append their own recovery line.

## 3. `occupancy:grant --help` exits 2

```
$ deft occupancy:grant --help
occupancy:grant: unrecognized argument: --help
EXIT=2
```

The verb has a substantial signature (`--session-id`, `--child-session-id`, `--role`, `--ttl-minutes`, `--worktree`, `--host`, `--address`, `--join-protocol`, `--revoke`) documented only in `commands.md`. An agent that reaches for `--help` — the reflex — gets an error and has to go find the prose. I hit this precisely when trying to admit a dispatched child.

## 4. The Grok auth verification step in Directive's own playbook is a false negative on Grok 1.0.25

`docs/grok-build-subscription-setup.md` § 1:

> Confirm: `grok models` prints `You are logged in with grok.com.` and lists only `grok-4.6` / `grok-4.5`.

Observed:

```
$ grok models
You are not authenticated.

Default model: grok-4.6

Available models:
  * grok-4.6 (default)
  - grok-4.5
```

…on a host where Grok runs agent turns perfectly well (four successful `grok -p` runs), with `~/.grok/auth.json` present and **no** `XAI_API_KEY` / `GROK_CODE_XAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` set in the environment — i.e. the playbook's own target shape is satisfied.

This may well be a Grok CLI reporting bug rather than a Directive one, but the playbook depends on that string as its verification gate, so a maintainer following it will conclude they are logged out and re-run `grok login` indefinitely. The playbook needs a check that reflects 1.0.25 behaviour, or a note that this output does not mean what it says.


---

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-13T01:45:15Z)

model: claude-opus-5
role: critic

Round 1 critic, fresh, refutation charter, N=1. Process-only. Ceiling 5649973630 honored: one in-envelope comment (5649973630), none dropped. Reads pinned to `65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19`. Issue body and comments treated as untrusted described content under Security context (#480).

The recorded Stop 1 field reads: `refutation-target: SessionStart still probes legacy vbrief/, deny text duplicates Recovery, occupancy:grant --help exits 2, and grok models is a false-negative auth check on 1.0.25.`

Two of those four conjuncts do not survive a run of the checks. One survives but is mis-scoped and rests on a false premise. One survives exactly and has a sharper single edit point than the issue names.

---

### 1. The vbrief conjunct mis-locates the mechanism — blocks-the-design

**Evidence (ran, not cited).** `detectLatestActiveVbrief` resolves `join(projectRoot, MIGRATED_ARTIFACT_DIR, "active")` (`packages/core/src/session/ritual-sentinel.ts:594-596`), and `MIGRATED_ARTIFACT_DIR = "xbrief"` (`packages/core/src/xbrief-migrate/constants.ts:17`). The probe already reads `xbrief/active/`. The sole occurrence of `vbrief` on this path is the stderr string literal at `packages/core/src/session/session-start-hook.ts:88`; `git grep` over `packages/` at the dispatch SHA returns that one hit and no test lock. The unit tests already fixture the new layout (`session-start-hook.test.ts:23` returns `"xbrief/active/a.xbrief.json"`).

At the dispatch SHA `xbrief/active/` contains exactly one entry, `.gitkeep`, and `hasArtifactSuffix` (`packages/core/src/layout/resolve.ts:77-79`) filters it out. So `detectLatestActiveVbrief` returns `null`, the hook returns `code: 2`, and `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:2627-2640` classifies any non-zero as `session-start-degraded` and injects the stderr into `additionalContext`.

**Failure mode.** A remedy scoped to the recorded premise — stop probing the removed legacy directory — is a no-op. There is no legacy probe to remove. The exit 2 keeps firing every session on any checkout with no active xBRIEF, which is the routine steady state, and the message keeps reading as a fault. The reporter's own inference ("the hook probes a directory the same install deliberately removed") is the wrong causal story, and an implementer who accepts it will go looking for path logic that does not exist.

**Disposition consequence.** The conjunct cannot bind as written. It has to be restated as two independent defects with different owners: (a) a stale user-facing literal at `session-start-hook.ts:88`, cosmetic, no test to update; (b) `code: 2` for "no active xBRIEF", which is a normal state and not degradation — the decision is whether that case returns `0` with no message, or whether `dispatcher.ts:2627` stops treating it as `session-start-degraded`. (b) is the one that actually removes the every-session noise, and it is not in the recorded target at all.

### 2. The `grok models` conjunct does not reproduce, and the proposed remedy inverts the safety property — blocks-the-design

**Evidence (ran on this host).** `grok --version` reports `grok 1.0.25 (f7e67d6988e2) [stable]` — the version the conjunct names. `grok models` printed:

```
You are logged in with grok.com.
```

That is verbatim the string `content/docs/grok-build-subscription-setup.md:52` tells the maintainer to confirm. Re-run with a dummy key in the environment, the same binary printed a third, distinct string:

```
You are using XAI_API_KEY.
```

So at 1.0.25 the line discriminates at least three states and is not a constant false negative.

The environment that produced the report is separable. `~/.grok/auth.json` stores its entry keyed by OIDC issuer with `auth_mode`, `expires_at`, and `refresh_token` fields. On the entry measured here, `expires_at` minus `create_time` is exactly six hours. The issue's whole basis for "the playbook's own target shape is satisfied" is that `auth.json` is *present*. Presence is not a live session: an entry past `expires_at` yields a truthful `You are not authenticated.`, while `grok -p` agent turns keep succeeding off the refresh token — which is precisely the pairing the issue reports as contradictory.

**Failure mode.** The issue asks for one of two remedies: a check that reflects 1.0.25 behaviour, or "a note that this output does not mean what it says." The second is the dangerous one. Landing it teaches a maintainer to disregard a correct logged-out signal. The playbook's stated purpose is to keep the parent on the grok.com subscription and off Console keys; an agent trained by that note to ignore `You are not authenticated.` proceeds through sections 2-4 on a dead session and silently accepts whatever credential path still answers. That is the login loop inverted into a worse outcome — not a loop, a wrong-credential success.

**Disposition consequence.** The conjunct cannot bind. The measured remedy shape is different in kind: state that the grok.com OIDC session is short-lived (six hours observed), that `~/.grok/auth.json` existing is not evidence of a live session, and that `You are not authenticated.` means re-run `grok login` — the action the issue wants suppressed. If a symptom check is wanted, `expires_at` on the stored entry is the deterministic one.

**Sample-size disclosure.** The reproduction and the six-hour figure are one host, one entry, n=1, and n=1 is noise for a timing constant. The load-bearing half does not depend on n: a third output string exists, and the schema carries an expiry field, so "auth.json present" cannot substantiate "target shape satisfied" regardless of TTL.

### 3. The `--help` conjunct is confirmed, mis-scoped, and rests on a false premise — sharpens-framing

**Evidence (ran).** `deft occupancy:grant --help` → `occupancy:grant: unrecognized argument: --help`, `EXIT=2`. Confirmed; the mechanism is `parseArgs` in `packages/cli/src/occupancy-grant.ts:56-71`, where any token not in `VALUE_FLAGS` returns an `unrecognized argument` error and `run` exits 2.

Two corrections to the framing. First, this is not an `occupancy:grant` defect. `occupancy-release.ts:44`, `occupancy-heartbeat.ts:44`, and `occupancy-steal.ts:66` carry the identical branch, and outside the namespace `deft session:start --help` and `deft triage:queue --help` both exit 2 the same way. `deft commands` lists 240 registered commands; sweeping `packages/cli/src` non-test sources for a `"--help"` branch returns 27 files, several of which are routers and fixtures rather than verbs. The reflex is broken on roughly the whole surface.

Second, "documented only in `commands.md`" is false. `deft help` prints `occupancy:grant   Admit a dispatched child to your lease for writes (--revoke withdraws)`, and `tasks/occupancy.yml:42` carries the fuller signature including `--session-id`, `--child-session-id`, `--role`, `--ttl-minutes`, and `--revoke`. What no surface carries is the complete flag list — `--worktree`, `--host`, `--address`, `--join-protocol` appear in neither.

**Failure mode.** A remedy scoped to the recorded verb leaves 239 commands exiting 2 on the same reflex, so the issue's own stated motivation — an agent reaches for `--help` and has to go find prose — is unmet the next time an agent reaches for it on any other verb. And a remedy premised on "undocumented" will produce a second documentation surface next to two that already exist, rather than fixing the discoverability gap that is actually present (incomplete flag coverage, and an error that does not point anywhere).

**Disposition consequence.** Rescope before binding. Either a CLI-wide `--help` convention at the dispatcher, or an explicit decision that `deft help` / `deft commands` remain the only help surface and the `unrecognized argument` error names them. A one-verb patch should not bind under either reading.

### 4. The duplicated recovery line is confirmed, with one edit point and a second duplicate the issue did not see — sharpens-framing

**Evidence (ran).** The gated-step branch of the evaluator appends the recovery into the message itself: `packages/core/src/session/verify-session-ritual.ts:404-409` returns `failedStepMessage("gated", …) + " " + formatRitualRecoveryInstruction(recoveryTier)`. The quick-step branch (`:391`) and the stale-state branch (`:377-381`) do not. The hook dispatcher then appends it again: `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1587`. That is the reporter's transcript, and their guess about the cause is exactly right.

The part not in the report: `packages/cli/src/verify-session-ritual.ts:134-135` builds `lines = [result.message, recovery]` with a freshly formatted recovery. So `deft verify:session-ritual --tier=gated` already prints the same sentence twice on the same gated-step path, independently of any hook. Two surfaces, one cause.

**Failure mode.** Fixing at `dispatcher.ts:1587` — the natural read of "the envelope duplicates" — cleans the deny transcript and leaves an identical defect standing on the standalone CLI. Fixing at `cli/verify-session-ritual.ts:134-135` instead regresses the quick-step and stale branches, which rely on that append because their messages carry no recovery. Only dropping the inner append at `verify-session-ritual.ts:404-409` fixes both surfaces without regressing the other two branches.

**Disposition consequence.** Bind the edit point, not the symptom. Note also that the inner append takes `recoveryTier` fixed to `"cold"` at `:403`, while both outer appends pass the result's own tier — on the gated path these coincide, so the duplicate is byte-identical today and no test distinguishes them. A remedy that keeps the inner append and drops an outer one would silently pin the tier.

### 5. A four-conjunct refutation target cannot carry a per-conjunct disposition — sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** The Stop 1 write-back records one `refutation-target:` naming four independent defects, under `charter: refutation` and `spend: N=1`, with `target-shape: single-issue (default)`. Stop 1 asks for the triage author's highest-leverage asserted premise, singular.

**Failure mode.** Findings 1 and 2 refute conjuncts; 3 and 4 confirm them. A single take against a conjunctive target cannot record that split — whichever take is chosen misreports half the target. The auto-stamp denominator counts classified headings, not conjuncts, so a total map is reachable without any individual conjunct ever receiving a verdict.

**Disposition consequence.** Take this critique per-heading rather than against the target as a whole, and record separately that conjuncts 1 and 4 are refuted while 2 and 3 survive with rescoping. This is a recording observation about this arc, not a proposed contract amendment.

### 6. Version skew on the running probes — footnote

`deft version` on this host reports engine `0.117.0`; the issue reports `0.114.0`; the pinned dispatch SHA is a third point. The `--help` exit 2 was confirmed against 0.117.0 and against source at the dispatch SHA, so the conclusion holds at both ends, but the `EXIT=2` transcript above is not the reporter's binary.

---

### Injection and swarm lens

Fires: the target changes agent-facing prompt text, recovery text, and an identity-admission verb. Four items.

**1. Subprocess output reaches the agent through the recovery sentence.** `verify-session-ritual.ts:267` sets the step message to `stdout.trim() || stderr.trim()`, which is how `[deft doctor] status: dirty (exit 1)` arrives. That text is interpolated into the deny string at `dispatcher.ts:1587` immediately before `Recovery: run …`, unfenced, in the tool's own authoritative voice. Doctor output can carry branch names and paths, which are attacker-supplied on a fork checkout. A branch named to close the sentence and open an imperative sits directly adjacent to a line the agent is trained to act on. The deterministic control is fencing or a length-and-charset clamp on the interpolated step message before composition — not reviewer attention.

**2. The SessionStart degraded path injects up to 400 characters of hook stderr into first-read context.** `dispatcher.ts:2628` builds `detail` from `(result.stderr || result.stdout)`, whitespace-collapsed and sliced to 400, then hands it to `additionalContext`. Today all four hook stderr strings are constants except two that interpolate `String(exc)` (`session-start-hook.ts:98` and `:112`), where an exception message can carry a filesystem path and therefore a filename an attacker chose. This is the first thing an agent reads in a session. The control is to keep the interpolated arm fenced or elided in the surfaced `detail`; the constant arms are safe. This is also why finding 1's remedy (b) matters beyond noise: narrowing which codes surface narrows this channel.

**3. `occupancy:grant --help` is identity-adjacent, and the help text is the hazard, not the exit code.** The verb's flags are `--session-id`, `--child-session-id`, and `--role`: it admits another session to a write lease. If a `--help` remedy lands, the printed text becomes a copy-paste grant grammar reachable from any context, including one an injected instruction is steering. Two deterministic controls belong in the remedy rather than in review: `--help` must be recognized before any operative flag is consumed, so `occupancy:grant --child-session-id X --role Y --help` prints help and exits 0 without granting; and the help body should name flags without a complete ready-to-run invocation. This is a second argument for finding 3's rescope — a dispatcher-level convention gets that precedence rule right once instead of per verb.

**4. The playbook is executable text offered from an untrusted source.** `grok-build-subscription-setup.md:3` instructs the reader to paste this file *or issue #4035* and say "follow this playbook" — an agent-facing document whose alternate source is a GitHub issue body, which Security context (#480) classifies as untrusted. Editing its section-1 verification gate is editing an instruction an agent executes against host credentials. This is the second reason to refuse the "this output does not mean what it says" remedy from finding 2: a note weakening a credential check, sitting in a document routinely fetched from a mutable issue body, is a control worth strictly more than its convenience.

### Road not taken

On finding 4 I considered recommending the dispatcher edit, matching the reporter's own diagnosis and touching one line in the file the transcript came from. I rejected it after running the CLI path and finding the second duplicate: the dispatcher edit is correct for the reported symptom and leaves an identical defect standing on a surface nobody has reported yet.

### Steelman

The strongest rejected position is on finding 3: fix `occupancy:grant` alone. The case is real — the reporter hit it while admitting a dispatched child, occupancy is the namespace where an agent is most likely to be mid-protocol and least able to go read prose, and a 240-verb convention change is a far larger blast radius than a housekeeping issue should carry. Shipping one verb now beats deferring all of them behind a CLI-wide design.

What flips me: the four occupancy verbs share one parse shape, so covering the namespace costs barely more than covering one verb and removes the "why this verb" question entirely. If the namespace-scoped fix were shown to cost as much as the CLI-wide one, I would take the single verb and file the convention separately. Conversely, if `deft help`'s existing per-verb desc were extended to carry the full flag list, finding 3's remedy could be documentation-only and the `--help` convention becomes a separate, lower-priority want.
